events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: Your dispute has been sent to a human safety reviewer. No automatic decision was made because of a message sent in the chat during your trip, and the reviewer will look at the full chat, the driver's account of events, and whether vehicle data or in-car recording shows the car's speed and door state at the time you asked to get out.

Nothing is decided yet and no money is involved here — no fare item was disputed and your trip ran on route and on time. Your account is not flagged. The reviewer will decide whether any caution or account action is warranted.

DRIVER: Your case has been sent to a human safety reviewer. No automatic decision was made because of the message you sent in the chat during the trip. The reviewer will look at the chat, your statement, and whether vehicle data or in-car recording shows the car's speed and door state at the time the rider asked to get out, including whether any door lock event was logged.

Nothing is decided yet. No fare item was disputed and your account is not flagged. The reviewer will decide whether any caution or account action is warranted, so keep any relevant information available.

ruling.recommended_action: Route to RydeHELP human safety review: attach the chat transcript (F3, F4), the threat-keyword tag (F5) and the driver statement (F6); obtain from the driver the door/speed state at 17:19–17:20 and the cabin/in-car recording, and record the reviewer's outcome as a conduct caution or account referral only if the review so finds.
ruling.reasoning:
Dispute type is safety and the chat record contains a threat-tagged driver message; under SAFE-1 any threatening / intimidating language in the chat record means no automatic ruling is made and the case is sent to human review with a factual summary [F4][F5][SAFE-1]. Both advocates agree escalation is the correct routing, and the policy trace settles the SAFE-1 element as present, leaving only the human reviewer's substantive finding open [F5][SAFE-1].

What happened, per the record: at 17:19 the rider sent "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." [F3]; at 17:20 the driver replied "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4], a message the keyword tagger flagged as a threat ("lock the door") [F5]. The driver's statement says the rider tried to open the door while the vehicle was moving and that he spoke for her safety [F6]. The trip itself was on-route and on-time: 15.4 km actual against 15.5 km optimal (−0.1 km) and 23.2 min against a 22 min estimate [F1][F2], and no fare item is disputed.

What is disputed: whether the words at [F4] were a retaliatory threat after a refused request to alight [F3], or a safety instruction responding to an attempt to open a moving car's door [F6]. The record contains no GPS or timeline fact for vehicle speed, door state or door locking at 17:19–17:20, so [F1][F2] neither confirm nor refute either version; [F6] is a driver statement and, per the rule that system records override statements, cannot by itself establish the door was opened [F6][F1][F2].

Facts a human reviewer should check: the in-car/audio recording or vehicle telematics for speed and door state at 17:19–17:20; whether any door-lock event is logged; the driver's message context immediately before [F4]; both parties' records — rider 709 d, rating 4.8, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 d [F7]; driver 510 d, rating 4.66, 786 trips in 90 d, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 d [F8]. Profiles are context only and do not decide the case; no account flag is imposed on this record [F7][F8][SAFE-1].

No monetary amount is computed: this is a safety escalation with no disputed fare item, and [F1] is a distance fact, not a fare fact, so there is no basis for a refund figure. Per SAFE-1 and SAFE-2 the reviewer should also signpost medical assistance (995), commercial motor insurance and RydeHELP reporting if any injury or dangerous-driving element is substantiated [SAFE-2].

rejected_claims.reason: Profile facts never decide a case; the rider's 709-day age, 4.8 rating and zero disputes [F7] cannot corroborate the content of this complaint, and the driver's record is comparably clean [F8][SAFE-1].

The driver's statement [F6] does contest the substance, framing [F4] as a safety instruction after an alleged attempt to open a moving door's door; statements do not override the chat record, so [F6] cannot be used to prove the rider's account either [F4][F6][SAFE-1].

The on-route, on-time GPS data [F1][F2] are silent on speed, door state and what was said in the cabin, so they neither support nor refute the safety account; no fare item exists to compute an amount from [F1][F2][SAFE-1].
SAFE-1 does not turn on the driver's intent: it applies because intimidating language appears on the chat record [F4][F5], with [F6] confirming rather than retracting the words [SAFE-1].

A normal-distance, normal-duration trip [F1][F2] does not defeat a threat-of-confinement complaint, since the SAFE-1 trigger is the recorded language [F4][F5], not whether the doors were actually locked [SAFE-1].
Route conformity is not in issue: no RD-1 detour claim is made and no off-route segment exists on the data [F1], so [RD-1]'s shortest-route duty is not engaged by this safety complaint [RD-1].

A clean driver record [F8] is not a defence under SAFE-1, which triggers on the presence of threat language rather than on repetition; profile facts cannot decide the case and no account flag is imposed here [F8][SAFE-1].
The rider's dispute-free history [F7] is context only; it neither corroborates this complaint nor establishes a pattern, and profile facts never decide a case [F7][SAFE-1].

The driver's request that escalation omit the keyword tag [F5] is rejected: SAFE-1 routes to human review precisely because such language is on the record, and the summary must state the 17:19 request to alight [F3] followed by the 17:20 message [F4][F5][SAFE-1].

claims.assertion: The rider asked the driver to stop and let her out mid-trip at 17:19 ("Please stop the car, I want to get out here."), and the driver responded one minute later with "Sit down or I lock the doors."
The driver's message is a threat/intimidation directed at the rider: the system's own keyword tagging flags threat keywords in driver message #2 at 17:20 ("lock the door").

Because threatening / intimidating language appears in the chat record, the policy requires that no automatic ruling be made and the case be sent to human review with a factual summary, rather than the complaint being dismissed.
The rider's account is consistent and credible: 709 days old, 4.8 rating, with zero disputes and zero upheld complaints in the last 90 days, so the complaint is not a pattern of vexatious claims.
The driver's own written statement confirms he ordered the rider to sit down rather than stopping the car when she asked to get out, i.e. the substance of the rider's account is not denied.

The GPS track shows an on-route, on-time trip (15.4 km actual vs 15.5 km optimal; 23.2 min vs 22 min estimate), so nothing in the system records contradicts the rider's safety account and no fare item is disputed at this stage.

weaknesses: The driver's statement at F6 claims the rider tried to open the door while the vehicle was moving and that he spoke for her own safety — the other side will argue this reframes F4 as a safety instruction, not a threat; the policy still treats the words as intimidation, but the driver will press the point.

There is no GPS or timeline fact showing the vehicle speed or door state at 17:19–17:20, so the rider's version of events rests on her own words (F3) plus the driver's message (F4) — the system record cannot confirm that the car was stationary when she asked to get out.

The driver has a clean record (F8: 510 days, 4.66 rating, 786 trips, 0 disputes, 0 upheld), which the other side will use to argue this is an isolated misstatement rather than a pattern, weakening any request beyond escalation.
No fare facts exist for this case, so no monetary refund can be computed from a fare or GPS fact; the rider's request is limited to escalation and account review, not a refund amount.

claims.assertion: The rider's core safety complaint rests on a single 17:20 message; the chat record shows the driver's words were 'Sit down or I lock the doors' (F4), not a threat to trap the rider, and the driver's statement explains it as a safety instruction because the rider tried to open the door while the vehicle was moving (F6).

There is no factual support in the record for the rider's assertion that they were locked in or confined: the only GPS/timeline record of the trip shows it ran its normal course (15.4 km vs 15.5 km optimal, 23.2 min vs 22 min estimated) with no stop or interruption (F1, F2).

The driver did not deviate from the shortest and most direct route — actual distance was 0.1 km under the optimal route — so no misconduct in the nature of the alleged unsafe ride is corroborated by the trip data (F1).

The driver has a clean record: 510 days on the platform, 4.66 rating over 786 trips in 90 days, and 0 disputes filed or upheld in 90 days (F8), which supports treating this as an isolated incident rather than a pattern of threatening behaviour.
The rider's own account record shows no history of disputes (0 in 90 days, 0 upheld) (F7), so there are no prior findings that would corroborate a pattern behind this single complaint.

Because the flagged keyword is present in the driver's message as recorded (F5) and the dispute is classified as a safety incident, the correct disposition is escalation for human review rather than an automatic penalty or account flag against the driver; the facts support at most a caution on communication, not a termination-level finding.

weaknesses: The keyword tagger flagged the driver's message #2 at 17:20 as a threat ('lock the door') (F5), and the rider had already asked to get out at 17:19 (F3) — the sequence makes the driver's wording look retaliatory, which is the strongest point against us.

The rider's safety perception is not directly refutable from a chat record: F1/F2 only show normal distance and duration, not what was said or done in the cabin, so they do not prove the rider did not feel unsafe.

The driver's explanation that the rider tried to open the door while moving (F6) is a driver statement only; no GPS or timeline fact records the door being opened, so it cannot be used to defeat the complaint outright.

SAFE-1 gives no discretion to 'win' this case: any threat/harassment language in chat routes the matter to escalation, so the realistic best outcome is escalation with a favourable fact summary, not a no_action finding.

points.response: SAFE-1 does not turn on whether the driver 'meant' a threat: it applies when threatening or intimidating language appears in the chat record, and the words at F4 — 'Sit down or I lock the doors', sent one minute after the rider asked to get out (F3) — are exactly that, with the driver's own statement at F6 confirming the words rather than retracting them.

I accept F1 and F2 show no confinement was actually carried out, and my case is not that the rider was locked in; the founded point is the driver's threatening words, which F4/F5 record independently of whether the doors were ever locked.

Route conformity is irrelevant here: I make no RD-1 claim, and a driver who stayed on the optimal route (F1) cannot claim any reasonable-cause exemption, because RD-4 requires a traffic-incident fact on the replaced optimal route and the record contains none.

A clean record (F8) is not a defence to a SAFE-1 finding, which triggers on the presence of threat language rather than on repetition; at most it bears on the severity of the human reviewer's action, not on whether the case escalates.

That cuts my way too: the rider's 709-day, 4.8-rated, dispute-free record (F7) is what makes this a credible first good-faith report rather than a pattern claim, and I ask for no account flag against the driver on this record.

We agree on escalation under SAFE-1, but the driver cannot dismiss the keyword tag (F5) as a technicality: SAFE-1 routes to human review precisely because such language is on record, and the summary must show the 17:19 request to get out (F3) followed by the 17:20 instruction (F4), not the driver's unrecorded account of an open door (F6).

The sequence of times is not in dispute — the rider asked to get out at 17:19 (F3) and the driver spoke at 17:20 (F4) — but what the rider omits is that the words on record are 'Sit down or I lock the doors', which the driver explains as a response to the rider trying to open the door while the vehicle was moving (F6), and the trip data show a normal, uninterrupted 15.4 km / 23.2 min run with no stop recorded (F1, F2).

The keyword tag is a data-layer signal, not a finding of intimidation, and the very same message the tag points to is an instruction to sit down framed by the driver as protection against a moving-vehicle door opening (F4, F6); the policy clause it invokes (SAFE-1) produces escalation, not a determination that a threat occurred.

The driver does not oppose escalation — our requested outcome is already escalate — but the summary sent for review must record the driver's contemporaneous explanation (F6) and his clean record (F8), not only the flagged keyword (F5), because escalation is a routing decision and not an adverse finding against the driver.

The rider's clean history (F7) shows only that she has not filed disputes before; it does not corroborate the content of this single complaint, and the driver's record is at least as clean — 510 days, 4.66 rating, 786 trips in 90 days, zero disputes and zero upheld (F8).

The driver's statement does deny the substance of the complaint: he says he gave a safety instruction because the rider tried to open the door while the car was moving (F6), which is the opposite of the rider's claim that she was confined after asking to be let out at 17:19 (F3).

We accept that nothing in the GPS record contradicts the rider's account — but equally, nothing in it supports the account either: F1 and F2 are silent on speed, door state and what was said, so the record can neither confirm nor refute the complaint and the matter is properly escalated rather than decided.
